claim: InferencePool is defined as a label-selector grouping of Model Server pods serving the same base model, conceptualized as an 'LLM-optimized Service' and serving as the discovery target for the Router -- i.e. the discovery mechanism is explicitly pod-label-based, not backend-address-based.
stance_target: identifying where the pod/Kubernetes assumption is encoded at the API level
quoted_support: The API that groups Model Server pods serving the same base model via a label selector. Conceptualized as an "LLM-optimized Service", it serves as the discovery target for the Router.

claim: A 'Variant' (prefill/decode role, cost profile, performance profile) is expressed purely through pod labels rather than a dedicated Kubernetes resource, meaning the sub-grouping mechanism used throughout llm-d for routing decisions is itself label-based and pod-native.
stance_target: extent of pod/label coupling in llm-d's core data model
quoted_support: Variant - A logical sub-grouping of Model Server pods within an InferencePool, expressed through pod labels rather than a dedicated resource.

claim: llm-d's Kubernetes-native autoscaling paths (HPA/KEDA) explicitly consume metrics exported by the EPP such as queue depth, coupling the autoscaling story to the same pod/metrics assumptions as the scheduler.
stance_target: breadth of k8s coupling beyond just routing (autoscaling also depends on pod-based metrics)
scope_conditions: llm-d v0.9 architecture docs, Advanced Patterns section
quoted_support: HPA/KEDA: Standard Kubernetes-native scaling using metrics exported by the EPP (like queue depth).
